catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue motion class fits this source. cap.motion.joint_position.v1 publishes joint positions in radians and requires per-binding joint travel limits, while the clone states no engineering unit and no travel range for PSISimplePositioner (the limits argument is optional at psi_positioner_base.py:91 and check_value delegates to the setpoint at psi_positioner_base.py:167-174). The extension publishes the axis position as UCUM 1, declares the target Limit.operator_required, calls the native move(wait=False), polls the device's own motor_done_move flag with cancellation checks, and returns the native MoveStatus success and a fresh readback.

cap.motion.stop.v1 was not usable: its optional deceleration input is inherited by the binding (the class schema has a deceleration property), and the native stop of PSISimplePositioner has no deceleration parameter to apply it to. The extension takes no input, calls native stop(), and reports the fresh done flag and readback. It is the declared safe_state action.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/bec-project__ophyd_devices --backend fake`; the last gate run printed the digest above and G1-G9 all passed with no warnings. Evidence is contract_checked and never an MHS-Device level. No hardware backend, EPICS IOC, ophyd, pyepics or upstream code was imported or run. Authored by model deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run helper-wave-1-010); reviewed_by is null and no human reviewed or tested this package.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper OphydDriver, but the Ophyd source proof refuses PSISimplePositioner. Its local base PSISimplePositionerBase has executable class-body values such as SIGNAL_NAMES = _SIMPLE_SIGNAL_NAMES (ophyd_devices/interfaces/base_classes/psi_positioner_base.py:74), sentinel class attributes and external PositionerBase ancestry; the other card entries are not closer fits for this driver: EpicsMotorEC and EpicsUserMotorVME have external motor ancestry and executable class bodies, SLSInfo's __init__ subscribes through a Signal method, and DelayGenerator rewrites suffixes dynamically. The package is therefore a direct Driver over the confirmed card entry symbol PSISimplePositioner (ophyd_devices/devices/simple_positioner.py:7), preserving the primary interface: fresh readback, setpoint, velocity and done reads, move, stop and e-stop.

Entry symbols were confirmed in the clone: PSISimplePositioner at simple_positioner.py:7, EpicsMotorEC at psi_motor.py:288, EpicsUserMotorVME at psi_motor.py:256, DelayGenerator at delay_generator_645.py:133 and SLSInfo at sls_devices.py:24.

Covered: position, setpoint, velocity and done_moving as fresh Signal.get(use_monitor=False) reads; x-cap.bec-project.axis_move.v1 over native move(target, wait=False), polling motor_done_move with self.cancelled() checks, a fresh readback and the native MoveStatus result; x-cap.bec-project.axis_stop.v1 over native stop() with a fresh done flag and readback, declared safe_state; @estop calls native stop(). The site overlay supplies the move target envelope through Limit.operator_required; without it every move is refused with MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. The site-limits.example.json target range -10..10 is an example site envelope, not a device fact; an operator must replace it with the measured travel.

Safety: risk R1, the card floor. The native stop is PSISimplePositionerBase.stop (psi_positioner_base.py:316-322): when the deployment configures the optional motor_stop Signal it writes stop_value to it; otherwise it reads user_readback.get() (the monitor-cache read, not use_monitor=False) and holds user_setpoint at that value. PSIDeviceBase.stop (psi_device_base.py:158-168) then cancels registered status objects. That is a software hold, not a hardware stop and not sensed quiescence; no independent hardware e-stop is declared, because the source names none and the card floor is R1. The runtime e-stop is a software latch plus that native stop call.

E-stop exercise gap: G6 passed, but its running-action e-stop case did not exercise a move, because the only move target is operator_required and G6 does not apply site-limits.example.json to that case. The move action checks self.cancelled() every 10 ms and calls native.stop() before raising Cancelled, and the fake moves 0.05 engineering units per 0.01 s tick (placeholders) instead of completing instantly, so a running action can be interrupted; this package does not claim that the stop is physically proven or that the axis is quiescent. A reviewer should treat the stop as a software hold until the deployment's motor_stop route and physical effectiveness are validated.

Fake: a source-shaped stand-in with the same public move() and stop() methods, Signal-shaped user_readback/user_setpoint/velocity/motor_done_move objects, done_value/stop_value and the stopped flag. All fake numbers are placeholders; it imports no upstream code. Fidelity is F0 and contract_checked; its 0.05 units per 0.01 s timing is the fake's, not the device's.

Hardware backend: native.py connect() imports ophyd_devices.devices.simple_positioner only when the hardware backend is loaded, constructs PSISimplePositioner under an operator-given prefix and name, passes optional native limits, deadband and override_suffixes, and waits for the Device's signals for at most connection_timeout_s. It was never imported or run. Deployment validation is still required for the real PV prefix and suffixes, whether the optional motor_stop suffix is present (otherwise the stop is the setpoint hold described above), the EPICS EGU (the driver publishes dimensionless UCUM 1 because the clone states no unit), native limits and deadband, and whether the native stop actually stops the axis.

NOT COVERED: any hardware run, the motor_stop hardware stop route, velocity as a write, the base report/position properties, real EPICS timing, and a running-move e-stop in the gate. No human review and no hardware review exist. The card and lock record BSD-3-Clause; this package makes no publication or licence claim beyond that card value.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation, every fact, the stop path and the fake against simple_positioner.py, psi_positioner_base.py and psi_device_base.py at the pin; the pass contradicted the readiness evidence (blocked) and does not hold. PSISimplePositioner declares no motor_stop Signal (simple_positioner.py:7-11) and override_suffixes cannot add one (psi_positioner_base.py:133-146 only warns for a Signal the class does not implement), so the author's configurable motor_stop route (a fact, safe_state, native.py and the notes) does not exist: stop() always writes the value read from user_readback into user_setpoint (319-321), a new target rather than a stop, yet it was bound as the e-stop and as a safe_state=True action and the e-stop reported completed. The fake hid this (its stop froze the axis and set the done flag at once) and reset the stopped flag on every move, which upstream only stage() does (psi_device_base.py:109-118), hiding that every move after a stop reported reached=false. The reviewer changed driver.py (the @estop sends the hold, then raises SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED; the stop action is an ordinary hold request without safe_state; reached no longer reads the sticky flag; safe_state, docstring, three facts corrected and three added), fake.py (faithful stop and move), native.py (docstring), test_driver.py (unreached e-stop, retarget and sticky-flag cases) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails only G6.ESTOP_FAILED and G8 SAFE-028 (stable digest sha256:229e13e513a8851df1f26ce5dea649c9e1838273c4b32844b84db95412e1e3b5), the eight package cases pass, and the author's notes on a motor_stop route and a passing gate are superseded. For the human reviewer: A generic EPICS positioner at R1 (card floor; payload and travel are deployment data, and the move target stays operator_required). The selected class has no source-backed stop: its only stop is the setpoint hold, which a motor record treats as a new move (it may overshoot and return), nothing senses quiescence, and whether user_readback.get() is a fresh read depends on the installed ophyd. The helper team's own BEC blockers (Status and callback lifetime, source identity; MHS/sdk/docs/ophyd-driver.md) remain. EpicsMotorEC and EpicsUserMotorVME inherit ophyd's EpicsMotor stop, which is outside the clone. Unit 1 stands for the unknown EGU. The move also polls motor_done_move right after the unawaited setpoint put, so against an IOC that has not yet cleared the done flag it can end at once with reached=false; the fake clears the flag synchronously.
